essay.en:
The surah opens with a threat: woe to the defrauders, who take full measure when they buy but give short when they sell. Tabatabai reads this cheating in weight and measure as corruption on the earth, of the kind God condemned through Shu'ayb, and finds its heart in people who demand their full due from others while refusing others the same [1]. Al-Tabrisi records that the lines came down when the Prophet reached Medina, whose people were then the worst of men in measuring, after which they mended their scales [3]. The surah then presses a question: do these people not realize they will be raised for a tremendous day, a day when mankind will stand before the Lord of all the worlds? Al-Tusi notes that 'think' here carries the force of knowing, though even a bare suspicion of such a reckoning should hold a person back [5].

A sharp 'No!' turns to the ledgers. The record of the vicious is in Sijjin; Tabatabai, weighing the word against Illiyyun, reads it as a place of confinement and descent, the recompense God has fixed and sealed for them [1]. The deniers of the Day of Retribution are named: only a sinful transgressor calls the recited signs 'myths of the ancients.' Their denial is not reasoned but earned, for sin has rusted over their hearts until they can no longer see the truth [1]. On that day they are veiled from their Lord, then driven to the Fire, then told, 'This is what you used to deny.'

Against them stands the record of the pious, in Illiyyun, elevation upon elevation, the high stations of nearness to God [1]. The surah lingers on their bliss: faces fresh with delight, a sealed pure wine whose seal is musk, mixed with Tasnim, a spring the ones brought near drink undiluted, since they outrank the rest [2]. It closes by turning the mockery around. The guilty who laughed at the believers, winked as they passed, and called them astray were never sent as keepers over them [2]; so on that day the believers, reclining on couches, laugh and look on - has the faithless been requited for what they used to do?

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: نزلت على نبي الله صلى الله عليه وآله حين قدم المدينة وهم يومئذ أسوأ الناس كيلاً فأحسنوا الكيل وأما الويل فبلغنا - والله أعلم - أنها بئر في جهنم.

text.en: It was revealed to the Prophet of God when he reached Medina, and at that time they were the worst of people in measuring; so they set the measure right. As for 'woe,' it has reached us - and God knows best - that it is a well in Hell.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Kazim
narrations.arabic: قُلْتُ كَلا إِنَّ كِتابَ الفُجَّارِ لَفِي سِجِّينٍ قَالَ هُمُ الَّذِينَ فَجَرُوا فِي حَقِّ الائِمَّةِ وَاعْتَدَوْا عَلَيْهِمْ قُلْتُ ثُمَّ يُقَالُ هذَا الَّذِي كُنْتُمْ بِهِ تُكَذِّبُونَ قَالَ يَعْنِي أَمِيرَ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ قُلْتُ تَنْزِيلٌ قَالَ نَعَمْ.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn Muhammad, from one of our companions, from Ibn Mahbub, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Hasan al-Madi

text.en: I said: 'Indeed the record of the vicious is in Sijjin.' He said: 'They are those who sinned against the right of the Imams and transgressed against them.' Of 'This is what you used to deny,' he said: 'It means the Commander of the Faithful.' I asked: 'A revelation?' He said: 'Yes.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: في قوله: { كلا إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجين } قال: هو فلان وفلان.
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Marouf, from al-Sindi, from al-Kalbi, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad

text.en: Concerning His words, 'Indeed the record of the vicious is in Sijjin,' he said: 'It is so-and-so and so-and-so.'

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: ما من عبد إلا و في قلبه نكتة بيضاء، فإذا أذنب ذنبا خرج في النكتة نكتة سوداء، فإذا تاب ذهب ذلك السواد، و إن تمادى في الذنوب زاد ذلك السواد حتى يغطي البياض، فإذا غطى البياض لم يرجع صاحبه إلى الخير أبدا.
narrations.chain: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Isa ibn Ayyub, from Ali ibn Mahziyar, from al-Qasim ibn Urwa, from Ibn Bukayr, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: There is no servant but that in his heart is a white spot. When he commits a sin, a black spot comes out in it. If he repents, that blackness departs; but if he persists in sins, the blackness grows until it covers the white, and then its owner never returns to good.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Rida
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى لَا يُوصَفُ بِمَكَانٍ يَحُلُّ فِيهِ فَيُحْجَبَ عَنْهُ فِيهِ عِبَادُهُ وَلَكِنَّهُ يَعْنِي أَنَّهُمْ عَنْ ثَوَابِ رَبِّهِمْ مَحْجُوبُونَ.
narrations.chain: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Faddal, from his father

text.en: God, blessed and exalted, is not described by a place that He occupies, such that His servants could be veiled from Him within it; rather it means that they are veiled from the reward of their Lord.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Baqir
narrations.arabic: إِنَّ الله جَلَّ وَعَزَّ خَلَقَنَا مِنْ أَعْلَى عِلِّيِّينَ وَخَلَقَ قُلُوبَ شِيعَتِنَا مِمَّا خَلَقَنَا مِنْهُ وَخَلَقَ أَبْدَانَهُمْ مِنْ دُونِ ذَلِكَ وَقُلُوبُهُمْ تَهْوِي إِلَيْنَا لأنَّهَا خُلِقَتْ مِمَّا خُلِقْنَا مِنْهُ … وَخَلَقَ عَدُوَّنَا مِنْ سِجِّينٍ وَخَلَقَ قُلُوبَ شِيعَتِهِمْ مِمَّا خَلَقَهُمْ مِنْهُ.
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Khalaf, from Abu Nahshal, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Abu Ja'far

text.en: God, mighty and glorious, created us from the highest Illiyyun and created the hearts of our Shia from what He created us, and their bodies from below that, so their hearts incline toward us because they were made from what we were made; and He created our enemy from Sijjin.

narrations.speaker: the Prophet
narrations.arabic: هو أشرف شراب في الجنة، يشربه محمد و آل محمد
narrations.chain: Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from his father, from Husayn ibn Mukhariq, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far, from Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Jabir ibn Abd Allah, from the Prophet

text.en: It is the noblest drink in Paradise; Muhammad and the family of Muhammad drink it.

narrations.speaker: Imam al-Sadiq
narrations.arabic: نزلت في علي (عليه السلام) و في الذين استهزءوا به من بني أمية، و ذلك أن عليا (عليه السلام) مر على قوم من بني أمية و المنافقين فسخروا منه.
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah

text.en: It was revealed about Ali and about those of the Umayyads who mocked him: Ali passed by a company of the Umayyads and the hypocrites, and they ridiculed him.

narrations.speaker: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn
narrations.arabic: إذا كان يوم القيامة أخرجت أريكتان [من الجنة]، فبسطتا على شفير جهنم، ثم يجيء علي (عليه السلام) حتى يقعد عليهما، فإذا قعد ضحك، و إذا ضحك انقلبت جهنم فصار عاليها سافلها
narrations.chain: Muhammad ibn al-Qasim, from his father, by his chain from Abu Hamza al-Thumali, from Ali ibn al-Husayn

text.en: When the Day of Resurrection comes, two couches are brought out and spread at the brink of Hell. Then Ali comes and sits upon them; when he sits he laughs, and when he laughs Hell is overturned, its top made its bottom.

perspectives.en: The sharpest divide falls on verse 15, that the deniers will be alienated from their Lord on that day. Shia hadith has Imam al-Rida deny that God occupies any place from which servants could be screened off; the veiling means they are shut out from their Lord's reward [67]. Sunni commentators turn the verse the other way: Ibn Kathir cites al-Shafi'i that veiling the disbelievers proves the believers will see their Lord [38], and al-Qurtubi reports Malik's reading that, because God veiled His enemies so they did not see Him, He disclosed Himself to His friends until they saw Him [44].

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: والتطفيف نقص المكيال والميزان، وقد نهى الله تعالى عنه وسماه إفساداً في الأرض

sources.gloss: Short-changing is to diminish the measure and the balance; God has forbidden it and named it corruption on the earth.

sources.author: Allamah Muhammad Husayn Tabatabai

excerpt.text: أن المقربين أعلى درجة من الأبرار الذين تصفهم الآيات

sources.gloss: The ones brought near are higher in degree than the pious whom these verses describe.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tabrisi

excerpt.text: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة كانوا من أخبث الناس كيلاً فأنزل الله عز وجل ويل للمطففين فأحسنوا الكيل بعد ذلك

sources.gloss: When the Messenger of God came to Medina they were among the worst of people in measuring, so God sent down 'Woe to the defrauders,' and afterward they set the measure right.

sources.author: Shaykh al-Tusi

excerpt.text: و (الظن) ها هنا بمعنى العلم، وتقديره ألا يعلم انه يبعث يوم القيامة

sources.gloss: 'Thinking' here is in the sense of knowing; the meaning is: do they not know that they will be raised on the Day of Resurrection?

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: نزلت على نبي الله صلى الله عليه وآله حين قدم المدينة وهم يومئذ أسوأ الناس كيلاً فأحسنوا الكيل

sources.gloss: It was revealed to the Prophet of God when he came to Medina, when they were the worst of people in measuring, and afterward they set the measure right.

sources.author: Ali ibn Ibrahim al-Qummi

excerpt.text: { كلا إن كتاب الفجار لفي سجين } قال: هو فلان وفلان

sources.gloss: Concerning 'Indeed the record of the vicious is in Sijjin,' he said: it is so-and-so and so-and-so.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: هو أشرف شراب في الجنة، يشربه محمد و آل محمد

sources.gloss: It is the noblest drink in Paradise; Muhammad and the family of Muhammad drink it.

sources.author: Sayyid Hashim al-Bahrani

excerpt.text: ما من عبد إلا و في قلبه نكتة بيضاء، فإذا أذنب ذنبا خرج في النكتة نكتة سوداء

sources.gloss: There is no servant but that in his heart is a white spot; when he commits a sin, a black spot comes out in it.

sources.author: Ibn Kathir

excerpt.text: قال الإمام أبو عبد الله الشافعي وفي هذه الآية دليل على أن المؤمنين يرونه عز وجل يومئذ

sources.gloss: Imam al-Shafi'i said: in this verse is a proof that the believers will see Him, mighty and exalted, on that day.

sources.author: al-Qurtubi

excerpt.text: وقال مالك بن أنس في هذه الآية: لما حجب أعداءه فلم يروه تجلى لأوليائه حتى رأوه

sources.gloss: Malik ibn Anas said of this verse: when He veiled His enemies so they did not see Him, He disclosed Himself to His friends until they saw Him.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: هُمُ الَّذِينَ فَجَرُوا فِي حَقِّ الائِمَّةِ وَاعْتَدَوْا عَلَيْهِمْ

sources.gloss: They are those who sinned against the right of the Imams and transgressed against them.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. yaqub al-kulayni

excerpt.text: خَلَقَنَا مِنْ أَعْلَى عِلِّيِّينَ وَخَلَقَ قُلُوبَ شِيعَتِنَا مِمَّا خَلَقَنَا مِنْهُ

sources.gloss: He created us from the highest Illiyyun, and created the hearts of our Shia from what He created us.

sources.author: shaykh muhammad b. ali al-saduq

excerpt.text: إِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى لَا يُوصَفُ بِمَكَانٍ يَحُلُّ فِيهِ فَيُحْجَبَ عَنْهُ فِيهِ عِبَادُهُ وَلَكِنَّهُ يَعْنِي أَنَّهُمْ عَنْ ثَوَابِ رَبِّهِمْ مَحْجُوبُونَ

sources.gloss: God, blessed and exalted, is not described by a place He occupies from which His servants could be veiled from Him; rather it means they are veiled from the reward of their Lord.
